title: Two Spoons, No Trophies, Now This
title_candidates: Two Spoons, No Trophies, Now This
The Nearly Man Who Never Trailed
Eighty and a Hundred and Seven
Neumann Goes First at Oitavos and Stays There
theme: A tournament of extremes on the Lisbon Coast — the field posting some of the biggest numbers in living memory and the lowest gross ever recorded at Estoril in the same four days — while the one man with no silverware to his name led it from the first afternoon to the last and was never once headed.
opening_hook: Open on the R4 scorer's table at Estoril, where the same short parkland course has just yielded an 80 (a new course record, Mullin) and a 107 (a new course-worst, Alex Baker) within the same five-man field — then loop back to Oitavos on R1 to explain why the Trophy had, by then, long since been decided in favour of Stuart Neumann.
foreshadow: Stuart Neumann's CV going in: no Trophy, no Jacket, two prior Wooden Spoons, and best finishes of 3rd (TEG 12) and 2nd (TEG 15).
Alex Baker arrives as the reigning Wooden Spoon holder (TEG 15) with two Spoons already on the sideboard.
Estoril's record book had stood undisturbed across six prior TEG visits — best 86, worst 106.
Gregg Williams comes in as defending Trophy champion (TEG 15) and, on gross, is about to be the best player in the field every single round.

headline_candidates: Oitavos Writes a New Worst — and Neumann Quietly Goes Five Clear
The Atlantic Rearranges Alex Baker: 113 and a Fresh Entry in the Book
rounds.chosen_headline: Oitavos Writes a New Worst — and Neumann Quietly Goes Five Clear
rounds.angle: Neumann's 39 points is best in the field and opens a five-point lead nobody yet takes seriously; Williams (89) and Jon Baker (92) both set personal bests at Oitavos; Alex Baker's 113 is the worst gross ever posted here across 12 prior visits, assembled from a 9 at the 1st, a 9 at the 11th and a 10 at the 17th.

headline_candidates: Troia, Unwrapped: A New Course Learns What It Is Dealing With
Neumann's Worst Round Is Still the Field's Best
Robert Trent Jones Sr Meets Five Men From Kent
rounds.chosen_headline: Troia, Unwrapped: A New Course Learns What It Is Dealing With
rounds.angle: A brand-new course for TEG, and Neumann's poorest round of the tournament (35) is still the best of the five, stretching the lead to seven; Williams bleeds through 8-11 and again 13-15 yet keeps the gross lead; Alex Baker drops to the foot of the Spoon race at the 13th and stays there for the duration, having shed 13 shots between the 13th and the 17th.

headline_candidates: Sintra's 12th Collects Its Tolls: A Ten, a Nine, and the Trophy All But Over
Williams Goes Five Holes Without a Blemish; Everyone Else Goes Down the Hill
rounds.chosen_headline: Sintra's 12th Collects Its Tolls: A Ten, a Nine, and the Trophy All But Over
rounds.angle: Neumann's second 39 pushes the lead to twelve and effectively ends the contest; Penha Longa's 12th — a par 5 marked SI 17, the second-easiest hole on the card — takes a 10 from Jon Baker and a 9 from Alex Baker inside the same hour; Williams pars five in a row from the 11th to seal the gross race, while Mullin's quadruple at the SI 1 16th caps a round 13 shots worse than his last visit here.

headline_candidates: Eighty and a Hundred and Seven: Estoril Rewrites Both Ends of the Book
Mullin Finds the Course Record Two Days Too Late
Neumann's Best Round Arrives With Nothing Left to Win
rounds.chosen_headline: Eighty and a Hundred and Seven: Estoril Rewrites Both Ends of the Book
rounds.angle: On Portugal's oldest course, Mullin signs for 80 — a new TEG course record, 14 better than his last visit — while Alex Baker signs for 107, a new course-worst, built on a 9 at the 1st and an 11 at the 12th; Neumann posts his best round of the tournament (43, and a 92 gross that is 14 better than TEG 15) despite a quintuple bogey at the SI 1 8th, and Williams closes out the Jacket with an 80 of his own in spite of a quadruple at the 14th.

players.arc: Two Wooden Spoons and no silverware in fifteen previous attempts, and then 39/35/39/43 — best in the field in the first three rounds, never worse than second in any, leader after every single one, and a first Trophy by 13.

The defending Trophy champion who was the best gross player in all four rounds, took the Jacket by 16 at +66 with personal bests at Oitavos (89) and Estoril (80) — and still lost the main event by 13, which is handicapping, not injustice.
Nine Jackets in the bank, a Penha Longa round 13 shots worse than his last visit and a quadruple at the SI 1 16th — then a closing 80 at Estoril, a new course record and a 15-point swing on his R3.

Personal bests at Oitavos (92) and Estoril (93) bracketing a Penha Longa collapse of 11 shots in three holes, including a 10 at the 12th, which is how a man with three Trophies and three Jackets finishes fourth.

The reigning Spoon holder was bottom of the field after every round, set new course-worsts at both Oitavos (113) and Estoril (107), and signed off with an 11 at the 12th — a third Spoon, comprehensively earned.

venue_notes: TEG's 5th visit to the Lisbon Coast. Use the courses as the shape of the story: Oitavos Dunes (3rd TEG round here, Arthur Hills links on the Atlantic) for the exposed opening; Troia (a new course for TEG, Robert Trent Jones Sr on the peninsula) as the unknown quantity in R2; Penha Longa (3rd TEG round here, mountain parkland in the Sintra hills) as the punishment round where the field's cards came apart; Estoril (2nd TEG round here, Portugal's first golf club, short, tree-lined, Mackenzie Ross) as the finale that flattered and humiliated in equal measure.
course_history_notes: Estoril's R4 rewrote both ends of its ledger in a single afternoon: Mullin's 80 beat the prior record of 86, and Alex Baker's 107 exceeded the prior worst of 106, across six prior visits.
Four personal bests at Estoril in R4: Mullin 80 (14 better than his last visit), Williams 80 (6 better), Neumann 92 (14 better), Jon Baker 93 (3 better).
Oitavos in R1 cut both ways: personal bests there for Williams (89) and Jon Baker (92), and a new course-worst of 113 for Alex Baker.
Penha Longa was where the ground gave way: Mullin 13 shots worse than his last visit, Jon Baker 12 worse, Neumann 6 worse, Williams 5 worse.

trophy_storyline.subject: Stuart Neumann's first Trophy, led from the first round to the last
trophy_storyline.why_it_matters: A man with two Wooden Spoons and no Trophy or Jacket to his name took the lead on day one and was never headed, winning by 13 on 156 points.
trophy_storyline.shape: Setup: Neumann opens with 39 at Oitavos, best in the field, five clear, and nobody treats it as more than an opening-day quirk. Turn: he simply keeps doing it — 35 at Troia is still the best round of the day and the lead goes to seven; a second 39 in the Sintra hills takes it to twelve and quietly ends the argument. Resolution: he closes with his best round of all, 43 at Estoril, absorbing a quintuple bogey at the SI 1 8th along the way, and wins by 13 from the defending champion.

jacket_storyline.subject: Gregg Williams's second Green Jacket, +66 by 16
jacket_storyline.why_it_matters: Williams was the best gross player in the field in every round of the tournament and still finished second in the main event — the cleanest illustration the players will ever get that gross and Stableford are two different sports.
jacket_storyline.shape: Setup: an 89 at Oitavos, a personal best there, puts him three clear on gross before anyone has settled. Turn: Troia is scruffy — six shots gone between the 13th and the 15th — but Mullin and Jon Baker cannot capitalise, and at Penha Longa Williams pars five straight from the 11th to blow the gross race open to fourteen. Resolution: an 80 at Estoril, his best there by six, seals it at +66 by 16, quadruple bogey at the 14th and all.

spoon_storyline.subject: Alex Baker's third Wooden Spoon, and the two course records he set on the way to it
spoon_storyline.why_it_matters: The reigning Spoon holder defended his title by sitting at the bottom of the field after all four rounds and leaving two courses with new worst-ever gross scores against his name.
spoon_storyline.shape: Setup: he is last after R1 at Oitavos with 113 — the worst gross posted there in thirteen visits — assembled from a 9 at the 1st, a 9 at the 11th and a 10 at the 17th. Turn: at Troia he drops to the foot of the Spoon race for good at the 13th, shedding 13 shots between there and the 17th, and Penha Longa offers no relief. Resolution: Estoril takes 14 shots off him in six holes and an 11 at the 12th, for a 107 that is a new course-worst, and a Spoon finished 4 adrift of his own brother on 127 points.

discovered_storylines.subject: Anatomy of an 80: Mullin's Estoril course record, two days after Penha Longa took him apart
discovered_storylines.why_it_matters: The lowest gross round ever recorded by TEG at Estoril came from a man who had, 48 hours earlier, played the same tournament 13 shots worse than his previous visit to Penha Longa.
discovered_storylines.shape: Setup: at Penha Longa, Mullin makes a quadruple bogey at the 16th — the SI 1, the hardest hole on the card — in a round that leaves him well adrift of the Jacket he has won nine times. Turn: at Estoril he birdies the 2nd, stops an early bleed with a birdie at the 7th, and then goes about the business of not dropping a shot — pars at 12 and 13, 16 and 17, nine points in three holes from the 11th. Resolution: an 80, beating the previous Estoril best of 86 across six prior visits, and a 15-point improvement on his R3 — a course record arriving precisely one round too late to matter to anything.

discovered_storylines.subject: The ledger of big numbers: nobody in the field escaped a quadruple bogey or worse
discovered_storylines.why_it_matters: This was a tournament in which every single player, champion included, posted at least a quadruple bogey — and the hole that did most of the damage was one of the easiest on its card.
discovered_storylines.shape: Setup: Alex Baker opens the account at Oitavos with a 10 at the 17th. Turn: Penha Longa's 12th, a par 5 marked SI 17, takes a 10 from Jon Baker and a 9 from Alex Baker in the same round, while Mullin makes 8 at the SI 1 16th. Resolution: Estoril finishes the collection — Williams a quadruple at the 14th on his way to the Jacket, Neumann a quintuple at the SI 1 8th inside his best round of the tournament, and Alex Baker an 11 at the 12th, the biggest single number of the four days.

payoffs.seed: Neumann's CV: two Spoons, no Trophy, best finish 2nd
payoffs.resolves_in: How the three were decided — the Trophy
payoffs.payoff: 156 points, leader after every round, winner by 13 — best in the field in R1, R2 and R3 and never worse than second in any of the four.

payoffs.seed: Alex Baker as reigning Spoon holder
payoffs.resolves_in: How the three were decided — the Wooden Spoon
payoffs.payoff: Bottom of the field after all four rounds, sealed at Troia's 13th in R2, finishing 4 adrift of Jon Baker on 127 points: Spoon number three.

payoffs.seed: Estoril's record book untouched across six prior visits
payoffs.payoff: Both ends of it fall on the same afternoon — Mullin's 80 (prior best 86) and Alex Baker's 107 (prior worst 106).

payoffs.seed: Williams the defending champion, best gross player in the field
payoffs.resolves_in: How the three were decided — the Green Jacket
payoffs.payoff: Green Jacket by 16 at +66 with best-in-field gross in all four rounds, and beaten by 13 in the Trophy — different measure, different sport, no paradox.

vehicle_fit_response.note: Taken up, but as the comic engine rather than the frame: Alex Baker's blow-up ledger (plus the field's collective 8s-and-worse) carries the humour, while the report is framed on Neumann's first Trophy after two Spoons.

why_the_champion_won: Built, not inherited: Neumann was the best player in the field in each of the first three rounds, beat Williams head-to-head in all four, and closed with his highest round of the tournament — even an ordinary round in place of Williams's worst would not have changed the result.
